question.text: A Category III AIF (determinate irrevocable trust) books FY25 income: INR 50 crore LTCG + INR 2 crore F&O business income. Under Section 161(1A) of the ITA, what is the risk that the tax department can assert?

answer.text: No issue — trustee taxes each head at its applicable rate because the trust is determinate
LTCG is recharacterised as business income automatically
Since ANY portion of income is business income, under Section 161(1A) the WHOLE income of the trust may be assessed at MMR in the trustee's hands as representative assessee
The fund is treated as indeterminate and taxed at MMR under Section 164

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 161(1A) specifically provides that where the income of a representative assessee INCLUDES any profits and gains of business, tax on WHOLE of the income of the trust is chargeable at MMR in the trustee's hands (subject to judicial precedent that concessional rates under 111A/112A may still gain precedence). This is the 'tainting' risk. Just INR 2 cr of business income can jeopardise the INR 50 cr LTCG concessional rate. The Trap: Option A is the ideal position but ignores 161(1A). Option B is a different concept (characterisation of income). Option D is the Section 164 indeterminate-trust rule, not applicable to determinate trusts. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B distributor exam rarely covers 161(1A); XIX-C treats it as a central fund-structuring risk. Manager's Pro-Tip: For Cat III funds, get an opinion early: segregate derivative/F&O books into a 'hedging' carve-out or use STT-paid cash equity exposure to reduce business-income taint. The 161(1A) 'all or nothing' risk is the single biggest tax pitfall for Cat III managers.
